title: Optimize Suggestions (Console) - preview demo
next_steps: Redwood to send a 1-pager explaining savings estimate inputs (baseline window, confidence, and double-counting rules) and the risk taxonomy (low/medium/high).
Customer to share a sample of their current traffic distribution (context length and concurrency) so Redwood can sanity-check batching/caching applicability.
Schedule a technical deep dive on telemetry requirements and data residency / RBAC (include HelioFin security).
Redwood to follow up on beta timeline for one-click apply + rollback workflow, and whether an API-based apply is planned.
body:
Fireflies.ai meeting transcript

Title: Optimize Suggestions (Console) - preview demo
Date: 2026-01-17
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes

Attendees
- Redwood Inference: Markus Klein, Evan Scott, Aditya Rao
- HelioFin: Priya Desai, Marco Alvarez, Jenna Liu, Samir Patel

---
Summary (auto-generated)
Redwood previewed the upcoming Console “Suggestions” view (beta) for batching and caching optimization. HelioFin focused on trust: how savings are calculated, what confidence means, and how “risk” is determined. They asked for more explainability (“basis of estimate”), reasons behind high risk labels, and wanted one-click apply with rollback and audit logs. Redwood confirmed beta is initially read-only behind allowlist/feature flag and walked through telemetry prerequisites and guardrails.

Topics (auto-generated)
- Suggestions list + detail drawer walk-through
- Savings estimates: baseline, $/1M tokens, monthly impact, confidence
- Risk levels: latency headroom, workload variance, reversibility
- Telemetry/data requirements and freshness
- Security: RBAC, audit logs, tenant isolation
- Phase 2: apply workflow + rollback

Action items (auto-generated)
- Markus to send demo screenshots + short Loom recap.
- Aditya to share draft “savings model v1” explanation and limitations for beta.
- Evan to confirm whether HelioFin can get per-route savings breakdown exported (CSV/API).

Questions (auto-generated)
- What window is used for the baseline cost and can we override it?
- Is “confidence” separate from “risk” or rolled up?
- Can we apply a suggestion to only one route/region and roll back quickly?

---
Transcript

[00:00] Markus Klein: Alright, cool. I think we have everyone? Priya, Marco, Jenna, Samir—thanks for joining. I’m Markus. Evan is our solutions engineer, and Aditya is the PM lead for Optimize.

[00:12] Priya Desai: Yep, thanks Markus. We’re mostly curious about the Console piece you mentioned—like, not just “set these flags,” but how do we operationalize it.

[00:21] Markus Klein: Exactly. Today’s a preview of the new Suggestions view in the Console. It’s in beta, read-only right now, but we want feedback on what would make you trust it and actually use it.

[00:33] Evan Scott: I’ll share screen. One sec.

[00:38] Evan Scott: Okay, you should see the Redwood Console. Left nav, we’ve got Optimize, and under that a new tab called “Suggestions (beta).” It’s feature-flagged and allowlisted per tenant.

[00:51] Jenna Liu: So it’s not generally available yet.

[00:53] Evan Scott: Correct. Beta cohort first.

[00:56] Evan Scott: The list view here is basically a table. Each row is a recommendation. Columns: “Type” (batching or caching), “Applies to” (route/model/region), “Estimated savings,” “Risk,” and “Data freshness.”

[01:13] Marco Alvarez: When you say caching, is that prompt caching or KV caching or both?

[01:19] Evan Scott: Good question. In this beta it’s primarily prefix/prompt caching signals plus some KV cache reuse where applicable—though the UI wording says caching and we specify in the detail drawer what mechanism we’re recommending. Aditya, jump in if I’m off.

[01:33] Aditya Rao: That’s right. We’re trying to avoid overloading the list. The detail view is explicit: “enable prefix cache on route X,” or “increase cache TTL from Y to Z,” that kind of thing. For batching, it’s more like “raise max batch tokens” or “enable continuous batching threshold.”

[01:51] Priya Desai: Okay.

[01:53] Evan Scott: Let me open one. Clicking a row opens a drawer. On the top: a one-liner like “Increase batching window for /chat/completions route in us-east to reduce GPU idle time.” Then we show “Why we think this helps,” “Savings estimate,” and “Risk rationale.”

[02:12] Samir Patel: Is any of this based on payload contents? Like prompts?

[02:16] Evan Scott: No prompt content. It’s based on aggregated telemetry—token counts, latencies, concurrency, cache hit rate if enabled. We do not ingest prompt text for this feature. We can go deeper on that, but the suggestion computation is using metrics streams.

[02:33] Samir Patel: Okay, so it’s more metadata.

[02:35] Evan Scott: Exactly. And per-tenant isolated.

[02:38] Evan Scott: So savings. We show it as “-$0.42 per 1M tokens (p50), range: -$0.30 to -$0.55,” and then “Projected monthly impact: $3.8k (based on last 14 days usage).”

[02:57] Marco Alvarez: That’s the part I’m skeptical about. Like, how do you know? Our traffic is spiky.

[03:03] Evan Scott: Yup. We try to reflect that with confidence intervals and by including the baseline window. Here it says “Baseline: trailing 14 days; includes weekdays only” — sorry, that’s a demo tenant setting. In your case it’d likely be trailing 7 or 14 days depending on volume.

[03:20] Jenna Liu: Wait, you can do weekdays only?

[03:22] Aditya Rao: Not a productized toggle. That’s in our internal sandbox. For beta, we’re standardizing on a baseline policy per tenant, and we will show it as “Basis of estimate.”

[03:34] Priya Desai: Basis of estimate is good. But I want it to be super obvious what’s included. Like, does it assume the same model? same max output tokens? Because we have some prompt templates that changed last week.

[03:48] Aditya Rao: Great point. The estimate assumes the same request mix distribution and same model version—like, it’s not predicting you change prompts. If the workload shifts, the estimate can drift. We’re considering a callout that says “Estimates may change with traffic mix.”

[04:06] Evan Scott: The drawer has a section called “Assumptions,” bullets like: “Traffic mix similar to baseline window,” “No change to model,” “No change to max output tokens,” “GPU type unchanged.”

[04:18] Marco Alvarez: And the confidence number—what is it? Like a statistical confidence or a vibes score?

[04:23] Evan Scott: It’s… not vibes, but it’s also not a strict 95% confidence interval in the classical sense. It’s a confidence score derived from telemetry coverage and variance. Aditya can explain better.

[04:36] Aditya Rao: Think of it as “how much do we trust the underlying signals.” If we have enough traffic, stable p95 latency, stable concurrency distribution, and the recommendation has been validated on similar workloads, confidence is higher. If your workload variance is high or the cache hit rate signal is noisy, confidence goes down.

[04:56] Jenna Liu: So then why do you also have “risk”? Isn’t that the same thing?

[05:00] Aditya Rao: That’s actually something we’re debating. Risk is “if you do this, what’s the chance of causing a bad outcome” — latency regression, quality regression, or SLO breach — and how reversible it is. Confidence is “how sure are we about savings magnitude.” They can be related but they’re not identical.

[05:22] Priya Desai: I like that separation, personally. Because I might be confident you save money but it’s high risk because of p95.

[05:29] Marco Alvarez: Or vice versa, low risk but unknown savings.

[05:32] Evan Scott: Exactly. In the list we show risk as a chip: Low / Medium / High. If I hover it, it shows a short tooltip like “High: limited latency headroom; workload variance high; rollback available.”

[05:48] Samir Patel: Rollback available means what in practice? Because if it’s a setting in your control plane, we need an audit trail.

[05:55] Evan Scott: For beta, read-only, so no apply yet. But for phase 2, the plan is an apply flow that writes to the same config system you already use for route policies. And we’ll log it in audit logs: who changed what, timestamp, old value, new value.

[06:14] Samir Patel: That’s table stakes for us.

[06:17] Markus Klein: Understood. We already have audit logging for config changes; Suggestions apply would hook into the same pipeline.

[06:25] Jenna Liu: Can we talk about the “High risk” thing? Like, it’s too vague. High risk why.

[06:31] Evan Scott: Yep, so we added rationale bullets. In the drawer there’s “Risk rationale.” Example: 
- “Latency headroom < 8% at p95 during peak hours”
- “High request-size variance (p90 context length 3.5x p50)”
- “Batching change increases queueing sensitivity”

[06:52] Marco Alvarez: That’s good. That’s the kind of thing I need to show to my manager.

[06:56] Priya Desai: But do you also show the actual numbers? Like p95 headroom calculation.

[07:01] Evan Scott: We do in a “Details” subsection, but it’s a little nerdy. It shows baseline p95 latency and your configured SLO target if we know it. If we don’t know your SLO, we infer based on historical p95 and what you’ve set in routing policy.

[07:18] Priya Desai: Okay, so there’s an assumption there. We have different SLOs per route.

[07:22] Evan Scott: Then we should pull per-route SLO from your config—if it’s set. If not set, that’s a gap.

[07:30] Aditya Rao: We’re also intentionally conservative: if we can’t determine headroom reliably, risk tends to move up, or we suppress the suggestion.

[07:40] Marco Alvarez: “Suppress” meaning it won’t show at all?

[07:43] Aditya Rao: Right. For beta we’d rather show fewer suggestions than show something misleading.

[07:50] Jenna Liu: That might be confusing though. Like, if I know I’m paying a ton, and it says “No suggestions.”

[07:57] Evan Scott: We have an empty state for that. It says either “No suggestions right now” or “Insufficient data to generate suggestions,” and we tell you what data is missing: “Need at least X requests/day,” or “Telemetry freshness older than 24 hours,” etc.

[08:14] Priya Desai: Telemetry freshness is a big deal. We’ve been burned by stale dashboards.

[08:19] Evan Scott: Totally. We show “Last updated” at the top and a freshness indicator per suggestion. If the baseline is older than N hours, we can show a warning and potentially stop showing the savings number.

[08:33] Marco Alvarez: Please don’t show a number if it’s stale. That’s worse than showing nothing.

[08:38] Aditya Rao: Agree. That’s a guardrail we’re adding: if baseline is stale beyond threshold, we show “Estimate unavailable (stale telemetry)” and we still might show the qualitative recommendation.

[08:51] Priya Desai: Okay. Next question: one-click apply. Is it going to be there? Because otherwise this becomes “nice to read” but not used.

[08:59] Markus Klein: You’re not alone in that feedback. The current beta is intentionally read-only because we want to validate the estimate model and avoid accidental regressions.

[09:09] Evan Scott: But phase 2 is apply. Likely a guided workflow: show the exact config diff, allow scope selection (route/region), then apply with a rollback timer and a “revert” button.

[09:23] Jenna Liu: Rollback timer like “if p95 gets worse revert automatically”?

[09:27] Evan Scott: That’s the ideal. We already have some rollout tooling—canary and fallback policies. The question is how much we productize for Suggestions.

[09:37] Aditya Rao: For the first apply version, we may do “manual rollback” plus an automated alert. Then later add auto-disable on regression signals.

[09:47] Marco Alvarez: We’d need at least canary. Like apply to 10% of traffic or one region.

[09:53] Evan Scott: Yep. The config change can be scoped. Also, for Dedicated you can test on a subset of capacity. For Hosted it’s more about routing rules.

[10:05] Samir Patel: From security: any time you “apply,” it needs RBAC. Like only admins can do that.

[10:10] Evan Scott: Absolutely. Separate permissions: view suggestions vs apply suggestions. And both are audit logged.

[10:19] Priya Desai: Okay. Can I ask about the actual math for savings? Like, I’m sorry, but we will get grilled on this.

[10:27] Aditya Rao: No, please ask.

[10:29] Priya Desai: So you show $/1M tokens savings. What’s the baseline? Is it our current effective price? Or some internal cost model.

[10:36] Aditya Rao: In Console, we’re showing your billed unit economics—what you pay today for that route/model. Then we estimate what it would be under the recommended serving configuration, using observed token throughput and latency impacts. For Dedicated, it can also incorporate reserved capacity amortization.

[10:56] Marco Alvarez: So you’re assuming the change improves throughput without worsening latency too much.

[11:01] Aditya Rao: Exactly. For batching: higher batch -> better GPU utilization -> lower cost per token. But it can increase queueing latency. So the model estimates both and penalizes if it would exceed your latency headroom.

[11:17] Evan Scott: And we show both pieces: “Cost impact” and “Latency impact.” In beta, latency impact is more of a risk explanation rather than a guaranteed number.

[11:27] Jenna Liu: That’s the trust thing. If you show “latency +12ms,” people will treat it as contract.

[11:33] Aditya Rao: Exactly. We’ve been careful with copy. We say “estimated,” “projected,” “based on recent traffic,” and we avoid “guaranteed.”

[11:43] Priya Desai: Good. Also—double counting. If you recommend caching and batching, can the savings stack? Because often they interact.

[11:51] Aditya Rao: Yes, and we’re addressing it explicitly. The model tracks overlap and avoids naive addition. In the drawer we show “Other related suggestions” and we label interactions. Like “If you enable caching, incremental batching savings may change.”

[12:07] Marco Alvarez: Nice. I’ve seen tools just add them and it’s wrong.

[12:12] Evan Scott: We had that bug internally at one point, honestly. We added tests for it.

[12:18] Priya Desai: Appreciate the honesty.

[12:21] Markus Klein: While Evan has this open—anything about the UI that’s confusing? Risk chip placement, the breakdown, whatever.

[12:30] Jenna Liu: The list is fine. I like the filter by route/model/region. We have multiple regions.

[12:36] Evan Scott: There’s a filter panel: route, model, region, suggestion type, risk level.

[12:42] Marco Alvarez: I’d want “sort by biggest savings” obviously.

[12:45] Evan Scott: Yep, sort by savings is default. Also you can sort by risk.

[12:49] Priya Desai: I would also want to export. Like, for a weekly optimization review, we want to pull a CSV.

[12:56] Evan Scott: Not in beta UI, but it’s on our list. The underlying API can be used for export once we lock the schema.

[13:05] Samir Patel: API access means auth, scopes, and rate limits. Don’t accidentally let someone pull other tenants.

[13:11] Evan Scott: Totally. Tenant scoping is strict, and we’d require the same RBAC.

[13:18] Priya Desai: Another trust point: I want to see “what changed since last week.” Like why did the savings estimate go down.

[13:27] Aditya Rao: We don’t have diffing yet, but we are capturing the inputs used: baseline window, traffic volume, cache hit rate. So we could add “Estimate updated because baseline traffic changed.”

[13:40] Marco Alvarez: Otherwise people assume the tool is random.

[13:43] Evan Scott: Exactly. We have a “Basis” section: “Telemetry used: requests=1.2M, tokens=410M, period=Jan 3–Jan 16, regions=us-east only.” That’s the sort of line.

[13:58] Jenna Liu: That’s great.

[14:01] Markus Klein: Let’s talk about your environment briefly, to see how these suggestions would land. Are you on Hosted API today or dedicated.

[14:09] Priya Desai: Mostly Hosted for experimentation. For production we’re considering Dedicated because we have predictable daily peaks.

[14:18] Marco Alvarez: We run a mix: embeddings plus chat. Chat has streaming.

[14:23] Evan Scott: Suggestions will cover both, but beta focus is chat routes where batching/caching are most impactful.

[14:30] Marco Alvarez: Our big problem is cost during peak. We can’t raise latency too much.

[14:35] Evan Scott: That’s exactly where the risk rationale is important. If you already run close to latency SLO during peak, aggressive batching will be high risk.

[14:46] Priya Desai: Do you look at p95 only? We care about p99.

[14:50] Evan Scott: In the risk computation we look at p95 and p99-ish tail metrics where available, plus variance. The UI currently highlights p95 because it’s more common, but we can include p99 in the details.

[15:04] Jenna Liu: Please do.

[15:06] Aditya Rao: Noted.

[15:08] Samir Patel: Security question. The “savings” reveals our spend patterns. Who can see this inside our org? Because we have internal separation.

[15:18] Markus Klein: RBAC. You can restrict access to Optimize views. In beta we’re making “view suggestions” permission explicit.

[15:27] Evan Scott: And access is audit logged: who viewed suggestions for which workspace. No exporting without permission.

[15:35] Samir Patel: Okay.

[15:37] Priya Desai: One more thing: what about model quality. If you suggest quantization or something, that’s risky.

[15:44] Aditya Rao: Beta scope is batching and caching only. Not quantization changes. Those have more quality risk.

[15:52] Marco Alvarez: Good.

[15:54] Evan Scott: For caching, risk can include quality risk in the sense of “stale cache” if TTL is too long, but we’re conservative and focus on safe prefixes.

[16:05] Priya Desai: Wait, do you cache responses? Because we can’t do that on personalized prompts.

[16:10] Evan Scott: No, not response caching by default. It’s prefix/prompt caching at the token level. Not “same prompt returns same answer.” Sorry, the term is overloaded.

[16:22] Priya Desai: Okay, that’s important. Please make that clear in UI copy.

[16:27] Aditya Rao: Yeah, we’re aligning terminology: “prefix caching” not just “caching.”

[16:33] Jenna Liu: Another UI thing: can you show “how to implement” in code? Like config snippet.

[16:39] Evan Scott: In beta we show “What to change” as a config diff and a link to docs. For example, “batching.max_batch_tokens from 8192 -> 16384” and “batching.max_queue_ms from 2 -> 4.”

[16:54] Marco Alvarez: That would be amazing. Also, what about the fact we already do some batching in our gateway.

[17:00] Evan Scott: Then the suggestion should detect that and either not recommend, or recommend aligning. We’ll need to understand your setup.

[17:08] Priya Desai: Our gateway does request coalescing. Not exactly batching at the token level.

[17:14] Evan Scott: Got it. Redwood’s batching is at the inference runtime. It’s different.

[17:18] Markus Klein: Time check—we have about 25 minutes. Evan, can you show a high-risk example and how it’s explained?

[17:26] Evan Scott: Sure. Here’s one: “Enable caching for /summarize route.” Risk: High. Opening.

[17:34] Evan Scott: Risk rationale bullets: 
1) “Cache hit rate estimate low confidence due to high prefix entropy”
2) “Workload contains many unique user-specific prefixes”
3) “Potential memory pressure; KV cache eviction risk at peak”

[17:54] Marco Alvarez: That’s really good. It’s not just “High.” It says why.

[17:58] Priya Desai: I like “prefix entropy” but we need a plain-English explanation too.

[18:04] Evan Scott: We have a “translate” line: “Many requests start differently, so caching is less likely to reuse work.”

[18:12] Jenna Liu: Nice.

[18:14] Samir Patel: Memory pressure: do you also show how much memory is available on the GPU.

[18:20] Evan Scott: In Dedicated yes, we can show capacity. In Hosted we abstract hardware, but we can show “observed cache eviction rate” and “OOM events” if any.

[18:31] Priya Desai: Okay.

[18:33] Marco Alvarez: For one-click apply, if you do it, it needs a safe default. Like limit to one region first.

[18:40] Evan Scott: Agree. We’re thinking default scope = one region and a short canary.

[18:46] Aditya Rao: And a “revert” button visible right in the drawer.

[18:50] Jenna Liu: That’s huge.

[18:52] Priya Desai: Also please don’t hide the limitations. Just say “beta.”

[18:56] Markus Klein: Yes, the UI has a beta label and disclaimers around estimates.

[19:01] Marco Alvarez: What about “realized savings”? Like after we apply, will it show whether it worked.

[19:08] Aditya Rao: That’s in our KPI plan. We want to show “before vs after” but it’s tricky because traffic changes. We’ll probably start with “directional impact” and tie it to a stable comparison window.

[19:22] Evan Scott: And we need the adoption signal: you applied it, or you changed config externally. Capturing that reliably is a work item.

[19:30] Priya Desai: Understood. But from a product standpoint, that’s what would get us to keep using it.

[19:37] Markus Klein: Makes sense.

[19:39] Samir Patel: Last security thing: data retention. Are you storing these suggestion details forever.

[19:46] Evan Scott: The system stores the suggestion record and the estimate inputs for a limited retention period aligned with telemetry retention. For enterprise, we can adjust retention and ensure it’s in-region.

[19:59] Samir Patel: Okay.

[20:02] Markus Klein: Let’s pivot to implementation fit. If we were to do a pilot, what would success look like for you.

[20:10] Priya Desai: Two things. One, reduce cost on the chat route by, say, 15% without breaking p99. Two, make it easy for platform eng to roll out changes safely.

[20:23] Marco Alvarez: And we need to be able to explain to leadership why we’re changing serving config. So the rationale bullets and basis are key.

[20:33] Jenna Liu: Also, I’d want to see confidence. Not as a hidden thing.

[20:38] Aditya Rao: Do you prefer a numeric confidence or just “High/Med/Low.”

[20:43] Jenna Liu: Honestly, just high/med/low is fine if you explain what it means.

[20:48] Priya Desai: Maybe show “coverage: good” or something.

[20:52] Evan Scott: Noted.

[20:54] Markus Klein: On the commercial side, if you go Dedicated, suggestions still apply—they’re actually more actionable because we can tune your capacity settings.

[21:04] Priya Desai: That’s appealing.

[21:07] Marco Alvarez: One concern: if you recommend increasing batch, will that affect streaming behavior.

[21:13] Evan Scott: It can. Streaming tokens are sensitive to queueing. That’s why streaming routes often have less batching headroom. The risk model factors in streaming fraction.

[21:25] Marco Alvarez: Okay. Because we do real-time UX.

[21:29] Evan Scott: Yep.

[21:31] Priya Desai: Another question: does the tool differentiate between Dedicated vs Hosted in terms of what knobs are available.

[21:38] Evan Scott: Yes. Some suggestions are “config-only” and some require capacity changes. In beta we’ll mainly stick to config-only suggestions.

[21:48] Aditya Rao: We also label “where it applies” — route/model/region — and “deployment mode.”

[21:56] Jenna Liu: Nice.

[21:58] Markus Klein: We’re coming up on time. Let’s do a quick recap of what we heard.

[22:04] Markus Klein: You want: (1) trust and explainability: basis of estimate, assumptions, and avoid showing stale numbers. (2) risk needs concrete reasons and ideally numbers (p95/p99 headroom). (3) one-click apply is a big value driver, but it must be safe: canary, scope control, rollback, RBAC, audit logs. (4) export/API and change-over-time would help operationalize.

[22:30] Priya Desai: That’s accurate.

[22:32] Marco Alvarez: Yep.

[22:33] Samir Patel: And security requirements: RBAC + audit trail.

[22:37] Evan Scott: Got it.

[22:39] Aditya Rao: I’ll send a written explanation of the savings model and what confidence and risk mean. We’ll include the telemetry inputs, baseline window, and limitations.

[22:50] Jenna Liu: That would be great.

[22:52] Markus Klein: Next steps from us: I’ll email a short recap, plus we should schedule a technical deep dive with your team, maybe 60 minutes, to talk about telemetry requirements and pilot setup. Sound good?

[23:05] Priya Desai: Yes. Also include someone from your security team maybe, because Samir will have questions.

[23:10] Markus Klein: We can bring in our security reviewer, or at least share the security packet ahead of time.

[23:16] Samir Patel: Thanks.

[23:18] Markus Klein: Cool. Anything else before we drop?

[23:22] Marco Alvarez: Just one more minor thing. In the UI, don’t call it “badging.”

[23:26] Evan Scott: (laughs) Yeah the transcript probably will. It’s batching.

[23:30] Priya Desai: Cool. Thanks everyone.

[23:33] Markus Klein: Thanks all.

---
End of transcript
